requirements.title: Criticality
requirements.text: How much the loss or disruption of the target would affect the organization's mission or operations.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: Loss has no significant effect on operations.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Loss causes minor disruption; operations continue with workarounds for days or more.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Loss reduces a key function for several days, or causes about a third of output to be lost.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Loss halts a key function within about a day, or causes most output to be lost.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Loss immediately halts the mission or a life-safety function.

requirements.title: Accessibility
requirements.text: How easily an adversary can reach the target, get to it, act on it, and leave.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: Not reachable without defeating multiple layers of detection and delay, with response assured before the target is reached.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Reachable only through controlled, monitored layers that delay entry and alarm.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Inside a perimeter, but in an area that is weakly controlled or monitored.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Outside the main security perimeter or reachable through routinely open entrances.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Openly reachable by the public with no barrier, control, or monitoring.

requirements.title: Recuperability
requirements.text: How long it would take to replace, repair, or bypass the target after it is damaged or lost.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: Restored the same day, for example from spares or redundancy.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Restored within 1 to 3 days.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Restored within 3 days to 1 week.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Restored within 1 week to 1 month.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Restoration takes more than 1 month, or the target cannot be replaced.

requirements.title: Vulnerability
requirements.text: How easily an adversary who reaches the target could damage, disable, or compromise it with the means likely available to them.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: Hardened; damage requires specialized means and extended time, and is very likely to be detected first.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Damage requires specialized tools or knowledge and significant time.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Damage possible with common tools and moderate time.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Damage possible quickly with common tools or simple methods.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Damage or compromise possible almost immediately with no special tools or knowledge.

requirements.title: Effect
requirements.text: The wider impact of an attack on the target: people, community, reputation, economy, and dependent organizations.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: No meaningful effect beyond the target itself.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Limited local or internal effect.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Moderate effect on people, customers, or the local community.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Serious effect on people, the community, or dependent organizations.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Severe effect, such as loss of life, regional disruption, or lasting loss of public trust.

requirements.title: Recognizability
requirements.text: How easily an adversary can identify the target and its critical parts without inside knowledge.

citation.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
citation.note: anchors are a Sentinel paraphrase adapted for facility assessments from the military CARVER matrix and the FDA CARVER + Shock adaptation; source tables not checked

anchors.label: 1 to 2
anchors.description: Cannot be identified without inside knowledge or expert help.

anchors.label: 3 to 4
anchors.description: Hard to identify; easily confused with other areas or equipment.

anchors.label: 5 to 6
anchors.description: Identifiable with some research or a site visit.

anchors.label: 7 to 8
anchors.description: Easily identified from public information or a casual visit.

anchors.label: 9 to 10
anchors.description: Identified at once by anyone, for example by signs, directories, or distinctive appearance.

name: CARVER Target Analysis
sourceEdition: Sentinel model 1.0 adapted from US special operations doctrine and FDA CARVER + Shock
publisher: Sentinel Assess (adapted from US Army doctrine and FDA guidance)
description: Scores each important asset or area from the attacker point of view: Criticality, Accessibility, Recuperability, Vulnerability, Effect, and Recognizability, each 1 to 10. Your physical findings feed the scores.

sources.source: US Army FM 34-36, Special Operations Forces Intelligence and Electronic Warfare Operations (1991), Appendix D, Target Analysis Process
sources.note: doctrine superseded; cited for lineage; not checked Library provenance: CARVER scores each target (asset, area, or process) on six criteria from 1 (least attractive to an adversary) to 10 (most attractive). Shared controls inform the Accessibility, Vulnerability, and Recognizability scores rather than satisfying them (see decision D-007). The anchors are Sentinel paraphrases adapted for facility security.

sources.source: US Army ATP 3-05.20, Special Forces Intelligence (current doctrine lineage for CARVER)
sources.note: edition and section to be confirmed
